narration: This is KubeSage, an AI SRE team for Kubernetes. Here is what is new, in under three minutes.

First, the summary. KubeSage puts FinOps and SRE in one system. It plans the savings, scales for the rush, and fixes what breaks. Small models do the legwork, and these runs cost cents. Every finding must cite evidence. Agent fixes are git commits. Plans and fixes reach the cluster only when a person applies them.

Picture a hypothetical online store on Azure Kubernetes. Five services share one node at two hundred eighty dollars a month. Two of them reserve two cores each while using almost none. Checkout traffic peaks every weekday morning, and sale days are bigger still. Tonight, a ledger cache ships with too little memory.

Sales are where FinOps and engineering meet. From thirty days of usage, KubeSage finds the weekday rush. Its KEDA rule adds pods ten minutes early. A CPU trigger catches surges no schedule predicts, like a flash sale. For a date like Black Friday, engineers add their own window to the same rule. KubeSage also sizes the node pool for the peaks it schedules.

Finding the waste is cheap by design. Statistics are free, and healthy workloads stop after one quick triage call. Only harder cases get more model reasoning. Guardrails floor requests from history. This whole analysis cost about one cent.

When an alert fires, four small agents gather evidence in parallel. Findings that cite no collected signal are dropped. A larger Thinker reads the rest, plus your team's plain-English rules, to find the root cause. An Executor writes the fix as a git commit, after policy checks limit each edit.
Here is the simulated cluster. Each glass is the CPU a pod reserves. Analyze estimates about thirty-four dollars in monthly savings, for one cent of model calls.
Apply right-sizes the services, moves them to the cheaper node, and adds the KEDA scaling rule.
Now a flash sale: sixty requests a second, replayed fast. CPU passes its target, and checkout-web scales out to six pods.
Then the bad release: ledger-cache runs out of memory, and the ContainerOOMKilled alert fires.
The team starts on its own. The sub-agents report, the Thinker finds the cause, and the chat shows every hand-off.
The fix is a commit: more memory, a proposal for a memory-optimised node pool, and two security fixes. Sixteen seconds, two cents. A person decides.
That is KubeSage: FinOps and SRE in one system, built for the rush, with a person in charge.
